title: granular-stamp-requests-and-quickpatch-playlist-2028-04-21
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recurring customer asks around per-request stamping/provenance + a short prioritized playlist of small fixes and probes we can ship in 1–3 sprints.

Context snapshot (why this doc):
- Over the last 6 weeks, CS triage has flagged ~28 asks that map to a common theme: customers want more deterministic, lightweight metadata attached to responses (trace IDs, model-version stamps, cost-estimates) and API flags to control whether that metadata is present, and at what granularity.
- These asks appear across usage patterns: high-volume embedding pipelines, multi-tenant inference (Dedicated customers), and Private deployments where auditability is required.
- Customers use terms interchangeably: "response provenance", "token-level stamp", "request trace", "model-fingerprint", "response-cost-preview". Need canonical defs before engineering work.

Raw clustered signals (examples + source):
- "I need a cheap per-response fingerprint so we can reconcile outputs with our logs when something goes wrong" — enterprise-fintech account (ticket RDW-2189).
- "Turn off cost metadata on high-throughput embedding runs; it bloats my logs." — analytics startup (Slack #cs-voice thread ts: 2028-03-23).
- "We require a signed model-version header that our audit system can validate for GDPR requests" — healthtech pilot (email chain, Confluence-REQS-1928).
- "When fallback happens (eg. model variant downgrade), attach the fallback_reason and variant_used so we can backfill evaluation" — large-gen AI customer (JIRA-RDW-3412).

Hypothesis / why this matters:
- Customers are balancing two tradeoffs: stronger observability (requires extra metadata) vs cost/ingest overhead (extra tokens, larger payloads, logging costs).
- No single default works; they want opt-in knobs at different layers: per-account default, per-route override, and per-request flag.
- Small surface-area changes can remove a lot of operational friction (reconciliations, audits, incident RCA).

Proposed canonical terminology (to standardize across docs & engineering):
- response_stamp: compact fingerprint for each response (<= 24 bytes string) that encodes model id, model hash, and request timestamp.
- provenance_header: optional structured metadata returned in response headers (json, opt-in) containing model_version, device_region, fallback_chain.
- cost_preview: small estimated token-cost field returned only when ?cost_preview=true; approximate, capped precision.
- signed_model_tag: cryptographic signature over model_version + response_stamp for high-assurance audits (enterprise only).

Quickpatch playlist (prioritized, low-risk items we can do in 1–3 sprints):
1) API: add ?response_stamp=off|short|full default=account-setting. Implementation notes: short=compact 24-char, full=verbose json header. Minimal change; route-level flag. Owner: eng-console. Jira: RDW-3412-1.
2) API: ?cost_preview=true (estimate only, not billed). Return field: cost_preview_usd_estimate (string). Toggleable at route-level; opt-out by default for embedding jobs. Owner: eng-serve-runtime. Jira: RDW-3412-2.
3) Console: Per-route toggle for stamp/cost_preview; update templates in console (checkboxes + tooltip copy). Quick UX: reuse existing per-route flags. Owner: product-console. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/682.
4) Schema: provenance_header schema v1 (flat keys: model_version, device_region, fallback_reason). Restrict size. Owner: eng-api. Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REQS-1928.
5) Private deploy: provide a bootstrap script that enables signed_model_tag using customer's KMS in 2-step flow (opt-in only). Scope: add docs + sample infra. Owner: eng-private.

Customer impact / ROI quick calc (back-of-envelope):
- Reduces incident RCA time by an estimated 30–50% for customers that adopt stamps (CS qualitative feedback).
- Logging cost reduction: per-request opt-out for cost_preview avoids a 0.1–0.5% token payload increase for high-volume embedding pipelines.
- Enterprise compliance wins: signed tags unblock 2 large pilots currently stalled on auditability.

Edge cases & constraints:
- Bandwidth-sensitive devices (mobile clients) will want minimal payload. Ensure default=off and use header-only short stamps for them.
- For streaming responses, attach response_stamp at stream start and provenance_header in final event.
- Signed_model_tag requires KMS integration and audit logging; scope is larger and should be gated behind enterprise contract + legal review.

Quick UX copy drafts (for console tooltips):
- Response stamp: "Compact identifier added to each response to help reconcile logs and debug issues. Off by default for high-volume flows."
- Cost preview: "A best-effort estimate of token costs for this request. For debugging only; not used for billing."

Open questions for follow-up (ask owners in sync):
- What is the canonical format for response_stamp? CRC-like short string vs base64 blob? (engineering to propose options).
- Should provenance_header be returned as JSON body field instead of headers for clients behind restrictive proxies? (product to advise).
- How do we surface adoption metrics? add checkbox telemetry + sample rate? (SRE + observability team).

Next steps / immediate action items (owners + timing):
- This week: eng-api to draft provenance_header schema and short response_stamp encoding proposal. Owner: Daniel Park. Target: 2028-04-28.
- 1 week: product-console to wire up per-route toggles UI mock and copy. Owner: Priya Nair. Target: 2028-05-02.
- 2 weeks: eng-serve-runtime to prototype ?cost_preview and short stamp at low-risk canary + perf bench. Owner: Miguel Torres. Target: 2028-05-10.
- CS: prepare 2-pager for the stalled enterprise pilots that explains signed_model_tag trades and timeline. Owner: Ava Chen. Target: 2028-05-07.

Notes to self / CS scratchpad (informal):
- Keep language simple for pilots: "signed tag" sounds heavy; earlier pilot contacts prefer "audit token" phrasing.
- Slack thread: #cs-voice has more raw quotes (search TS 2028-03 to 2028-04).
- Link to RDW-3412 parent ticket for tracking the engineering epic.

Minimal risk rollout plan idea (for discussion):
- Phase 0: internal canary — enable short response_stamp for internal Redwood accounts + SRE team; measure overhead.
- Phase 1: opt-in customers — release flags to customers in beta; default off for all.
- Phase 2: GA — enable per-account defaults and console toggles + docs + SDK examples.

Appendix: sketch of response_stamp encoding (brain dump):
- version (1 byte) | model_hash (8 bytes truncated) | timestamp (4 bytes epoch) | small CRC (2 bytes) => base64url => ~20 chars.
- Full JSON verbose stamp example: {"model_version":"redwood-open-1.3","model_hash":"ab12cd34","timestamp":1682000000,"fallback_chain":["open-1.3"]}

If you disagree with any prioritization or want to add low-risk items (eg. event-level telemetry flag), drop a comment below or add to the linked ARCH ticket: JIRA-RDW-3412.
